findings.claim: The requirement says MessagePack attributes on T must be honoured, and ledger L19 says to follow it. When no SurrogateType is set, Collect always takes the contractless path and never checks T for [MessagePackObject]/[Key]. So a referenced-assembly T declared `[MessagePackObject] class MyType { [Key(0)] public int A {get;set;} [Key(1)] public string B {get;set;} }` gets a string-keyed map formatter ("A", "B") instead of the int-keyed array contract it declares. The result is a wire format incompatible with every other MessagePack serializer of that type.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterHonoursAttributesTests.ReferencedTypeWithIntKeysProducesArrayFormatter. It compiles ProjectA with [MessagePackObject]/[Key(0)]/[Key(1)] into a metadata reference, then runs MessagePackGenerator on ProjectB containing [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class MyTypeFormatter : IMessagePackFormatter<ProjectA.MyType>. It asserts the generated formatter uses WriteArrayHeader and not WriteMapHeader. On head it emits a map/string-key formatter, so the test fails.

findings.claim: In surrogate mode, every instance field or property of the surrogate that lacks [Key] and [IgnoreMember] is rejected with MemberNeedsKey, including private ones. A surrogate with `private int helper;` beside `[Key(0)] public int A {get;set;}` therefore fails generation. The existing MsgPack004 rule (L5) only demands keys on public members.

receipt_plan.detail: Generator-driver test: surrogate class with a private unkeyed field plus one [Key(0)] public property matching T. Expect a formatter to be emitted and no MsgPack004/005 diagnostic; on head the diagnostic is produced and no formatter is emitted.

findings.claim: Nothing checks whether two [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] classes target the same T. It is also not checked whether T is a source [MessagePackObject] type that TypeCollector already generates a formatter for. Both ObjectSerializationInfos are added to the model, so the generated resolver registers the same data type twice: a duplicate key in the type-to-formatter map, or one formatter silently dropped. No diagnostic is reported.

receipt_plan.detail: Generator-driver test: declare `[MessagePackObject] public class T { [Key(0)] public int A {get;set;} }` and `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class TF : IMessagePackFormatter<T> {}` plus a resolver. Compile the generated output and call GeneratedResolver.Instance.GetFormatter<T>(). Expect either a diagnostic or a single registration; on head expect a duplicate registration (compile error or ArgumentException in the resolver's static initializer).
